report:
Reviewed the complete shared_final_result claim and both implementation entries, and both test entries after associating the existing substantive whiteboard test. Requirements: a frame owns one producer for its canonical atomic request; subscribers receive one shared terminal result; candidate/frame progress is revisioned side information rather than additional Future outputs or raw candidate state; continuations remain Rust futures with bounded polling rounds.

The ordinary prove.rs entry is supported by ProofFrame, Whiteboard::request/complete, ProofFuture::poll and solve_query in its captured whole-file context. request keys frames by canonical query plus parent/depth context, allocates separate subscription IDs, and uses producer_started and the single producer slot to prevent duplicate producer creation. Pending requests reuse that frame; ready requests clone the saved result. complete accepts only Pending, installs one Ready value and drains subscriber wakers. ProofFuture has only Stashed<QueryResult> as output and only Pending or Ready observations; it has no candidate-state reference or intermediate-result variant. Candidate async blocks own their state and return answers within solve_trait_frame/solve_normalize_frame; that candidate work is not published directly through subscriptions. ProducerFuture and prove_goal explicitly retain pinned boxed Rust futures. These are structural ownership/output observations; this review does not claim correctness of unification, candidate selection, canonicalization or merge algorithms, which are separate claims.

The now-associated ordinary test same_parent_requests_share_one_live_producer_and_result exercises an atomic equality query with two live subscribers, asserts equal FrameId and subscription count two, awaits both and asserts identical responses, then verifies ready-cache reuse and equality with the original result. It asserts exactly one frame, Ready state, and an empty subscription set. Setup helpers with_crate, make_test_crate and equality_query are in the captured prove.rs file. The test would detect separate frames/results or stale subscriptions and meaningfully covers implemented shared terminal publication.

The semantic_spec TODO implementation explicitly defers bounded polling rounds and monotone intermediate publication. The associated solver_shared_final_result TODO test has no assertions and supplies no behavioral evidence. Its intended remaining matrix covers candidate-state non-observation, monotone snapshots and self-waking pending work not starving siblings. These prerequisites are justified: current ProofFrame has no progress/revision channel, and drive drains a runnable queue rather than establishing a bounded round snapshot. Future bounded-round scheduling and revisioned progress publication are required before those scenarios can be tested as implemented. Accepting these explicit TODOs preserves their deferred status; the existing test covers the already available duplicate-requester slice, not the progress/scheduling extension. No N/A entries exist. All claim aspects are therefore accounted for by substantive implementation/test evidence or explicit existing deferral.

Executed cargo fmt and cargo test -p sage-ir same_parent_requests_share_one_live_producer_and_result: one test passed. Review start/read captured fresh inputs after the annotation change; no behavioral production changes or new regression expectation were introduced. Workspace build and centralized delegated post-codegen/sanity checks are coordinated with the main agent, and are separate from this source adequacy verdict.
